papers.title: Super high strength of annealed Fe32Cr33Ni29Al3Ti3 manufactured by selective laser melting
papers.abstract: Selective laser melting (SLM) of high entropy alloys (HEAs) shows great potential in industry applications and annealing was always used as a post-processing method after SLM. A dual-phase (DP) Co-free HEA was manufactured by SLM and annealed at 900 °C in this work. The annealed HEA exhibited super high yield and tensile strengths (∼1224 and ∼1363 MPa, respectively), higher than those of the as-printed sample, primarily attributed to grain refinement and spinodal decomposition with FCC phase (rich in Ni/Al/Ti) and BCC phase (rich in Cr/Fe) decomposing into FCC (rich in Fe), B2 (rich in Cr, poor in Ni), and L1 2 (rich in Ni/Al/Ti, poor in Fe/Cr) during annealing. The annealed DP Co-free HEA exhibits notably superior strength to other Co-free HEAs or medium entropy alloys (MEAs) produced via SLM. Due to their affordability, Co-free HEAs show immense potential for widespread commercial use, and this study explores annealing in SLM to improve the mechanical properties of HEAs. The high-strength annealed DP Co-free HEA could be especially valuable for structural elements in construction applications. • Super high strength ever reported in SLM-processed Co-free HEAs or MEAS: The annealed Co-free HEA has a strength (yield strength ∼1224 and tensile strength ∼1363 MPa) higher than the as-printed sample (yield strength ∼857 and tensile strength ∼1207 MPa) and other reported SLM- processed Co-free HEAs or MEAs. Due to their affordability, Co-free HEAs show immense potential for widespread commercial use and this work shows its significance. • Unique elemental segregation: TEM results show that spinodal decomposition occurred with FCC phase (rich in Ni/Al/Ti) and BCC phase (rich in Cr/Fe) decomposing into FCC (rich in Fe), B2 (rich in Cr, poor in Ni), and L1 2 (rich in Ni/Al/Ti, poor in Fe/Cr) during annealing. This Co-free dual-phase HEA shows unique elemental segregation with element distribution that is quite different from other dual-phase HEAs, for example, AlCoCrFeNi2.1. • Strength increased after annealing at 900 °C: Different from other research with strength decreasing after annealing treatments at a temperature of 900 °C, the strength of the annealed Co-free dual-phase HEA (Fe32Cr33Ni29Al3Ti3) increased due to grain refinement and spinodal decomposition resulting in various strengthening mechanisms.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究的是SLM制备的钴-free高熵合金的退火强化，未涉及生物医学植入物、多孔结构、应力遮挡或骨整合。
llm.why_not_core: No biomedical implant context, no porous structure, no stress shielding or stiffness matching analysis, no fatigue testing, no surface roughness or osseointegration evaluation.

summary_zh.motivation: 提高SLM制备钴-free高熵合金的强度，探索退火后处理效果。
summary_zh.method: 采用SLM制备Fe32Cr33Ni29Al3Ti3，900°C退火后表征微观结构和力学性能。
summary_zh.result: 退火后合金屈服强度达1224 MPa，抗拉强度1363 MPa，优于同类材料。
summary_zh.validation: 通过拉伸测试和TEM微观分析验证性能提升和相分解机制。

summary_en.motivation: To enhance the mechanical strength of Co-free high-entropy alloys fabricated by selective laser melting via post-process annealing.
summary_en.method: Fe32Cr33Ni29Al3Ti3 was fabricated by SLM and annealed at 900°C; microstructure and tensile properties were characterized.
summary_en.result: Annealed alloy achieved a yield strength of ~1224 MPa and tensile strength of ~1363 MPa, outperforming other SLM-processed Co-free HEAs.
summary_en.validation: Tensile testing and TEM analysis confirmed strength enhancement due to grain refinement and spinodal decomposition.

papers.title: Tailored Finite Point Operator Networks for Interface problems
papers.abstract: Interface problems pose significant challenges due to the discontinuity of their solutions, particularly when they involve singular perturbations or high-contrast coefficients, resulting in intricate singularities that complicate resolution. The increasing adoption of deep learning techniques for solving partial differential equations has spurred our exploration of these methods for addressing interface problems. In this study, we introduce Tailored Finite Point Operator Networks (TFPONets) as a novel approach for tackling parameterized interface problems. Leveraging DeepONets and integrating the Tailored Finite Point method (TFPM), TFPONets offer enhanced accuracy in reconstructing solutions without the need for intricate equation manipulation. Experimental analyses conducted in both one- and two-dimensional scenarios reveal that, in comparison to existing methods such as DeepONet and IONet, TFPONets demonstrate superior learning and generalization capabilities even with limited locations.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文提出了一种针对界面问题的算子网络方法，可迁移至生物力学中的多材料界面问题，但未涉及植入物设计或不确定性量化。
llm.why_not_core: No validation on implant/biomechanics problems, no uncertainty quantification, and no handling of constraints or multi-objective optimization.

summary_zh.motivation: 界面问题因解不连续而难以求解，传统方法复杂。
summary_zh.method: 结合DeepONet与Tailored Finite Point方法，提出TFPONets。
summary_zh.result: 在1D和2D界面问题上，TFPONets比DeepONet和IONet泛化能力更强。
summary_zh.validation: 在数值基准算例上验证，包括高对比系数和奇异摄动问题。

summary_en.motivation: Interface problems with discontinuous solutions and singularities are challenging for traditional solvers, motivating the use of deep learning.
summary_en.method: TFPONets integrate the Tailored Finite Point method into the DeepONet framework to handle parameterized interface problems without complex equation manipulation.
summary_en.result: TFPONets achieve superior learning and generalization compared to DeepONet and IONet on 1D and 2D interface benchmarks.
summary_en.validation: Numerical experiments on 1D and 2D interface problems with high-contrast coefficients and singular perturbations.

papers.title: Component Fourier Neural Operator for Singularly Perturbed Differential Equations
papers.abstract: Solving Singularly Perturbed Differential Equations (SPDEs) poses computational challenges arising from the rapid transitions in their solutions within thin regions. The effectiveness of deep learning in addressing differential equations motivates us to employ these methods for solving SPDEs. In this manuscript, we introduce Component Fourier Neural Operator (ComFNO), an innovative operator learning method that builds upon Fourier Neural Operator (FNO), while simultaneously incorporating valuable prior knowledge obtained from asymptotic analysis. Our approach is not limited to FNO and can be applied to other neural network frameworks, such as Deep Operator Network (DeepONet), leading to potential similar SPDEs solvers. Experimental results across diverse classes of SPDEs demonstrate that ComFNO significantly improves accuracy compared to vanilla FNO. Furthermore, ComFNO exhibits natural adaptability to diverse data distributions and performs well in few-shot scenarios, showcasing its excellent generalization ability in practical situations.

summary_en.motivation: Solving singularly perturbed differential equations is computationally challenging due to rapid solution transitions in thin regions.
summary_en.method: We propose Component Fourier Neural Operator (ComFNO), which incorporates prior knowledge from asymptotic analysis into the Fourier Neural Operator framework.
summary_en.result: ComFNO significantly improves accuracy over vanilla FNO and demonstrates strong generalization in few-shot scenarios across diverse SPDEs.
summary_en.validation: Numerical benchmarks on various classes of singularly perturbed differential equations.

papers.title: Harnessing physics-informed operators for high-dimensional reliability analysis problems
papers.abstract: Reliability analysis is a formidable task, particularly in systems with a large number of stochastic parameters. Conventional methods for quantifying reliability often rely on extensive simulations or experimental data, which can be costly and time-consuming, especially when dealing with systems governed by complex physical laws which necessitates computationally intensive numerical methods such as finite element or finite volume techniques. On the other hand, surrogate-based methods offer an efficient alternative for computing reliability by approximating the underlying model from limited data. Neural operators have recently emerged as effective surrogates for modelling physical systems governed by partial differential equations. These operators can learn solutions to PDEs for varying inputs and parameters. Here, we investigate the efficacy of the recently developed physics-informed wavelet neural operator in solving reliability analysis problems. In particular, we investigate the possibility of using physics-informed operator for solving high-dimensional reliability analysis problems, while bypassing the need for any simulation. Through four numerical examples, we illustrate that physics-informed operator can seamlessly solve high-dimensional reliability analysis problems with reasonable accuracy, while eliminating the need for running expensive simulations.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文提出的物理信息算子方法可直接迁移至生物力学植入物设计中的高维可靠性分析，解决昂贵仿真采样效率问题。
llm.why_not_core: The paper does not apply the method to implant/biomechanics design, lacks constraint handling, and does not include uncertainty quantification beyond reliability probability.

summary_zh.motivation: 高维可靠性分析中传统方法计算成本高，需要高效替代模型。
summary_zh.method: 采用物理信息小波神经算子作为替代模型，无需仿真数据直接求解可靠性。
summary_zh.result: 在四个数值算例中，该方法以合理精度求解高维可靠性问题，避免了昂贵仿真。
summary_zh.validation: 通过四个数值算例验证，与参考解对比精度。

summary_en.motivation: Reliability analysis for high-dimensional stochastic systems is computationally prohibitive using conventional simulation-based methods.
summary_en.method: A physics-informed wavelet neural operator is employed as a surrogate to directly solve reliability problems without any simulation data.
summary_en.result: The proposed operator achieves reasonable accuracy on four numerical benchmarks while eliminating the need for expensive simulations.
summary_en.validation: Validation is performed on four numerical examples with known reference solutions.
